doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Gloria Lynne, Milt Hinton and later work
title: Broadway's Sophisticated Ladies and Duke Ellington
summary: May recalls the Broadway show band and road trip, with a story about Duke telling a sideman to just play.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well you’ve come a long way since the violin. You did some work with the “Sophisticated Lady” show.

Oh yeah, that was another wonderful experience of mine, just being on Broadway with that band and playing all that good music with all those wonderful people on stage. It was wonderful. And then going on the road with them was so nice. I had a wonderful time with that. We bonded, and we’d get on the bus and slap and giggle and you know, it was wonderful. I really had a good time. I got in a lot of income tax trouble over that, I’m still suffering from it, but other than that it was a wonderful experience. Duke was absolutely

incredible. Really amazing. And there was a story going around where I don’t remember who the players were but this guy had just joined the band and he was saying — he stopped the band at one time, I don’t know if they were rehearsing for a show or what — and he says, “Duke, you got this saxophone player playing F and you got me playing F sharp.” And Duke says, “Just play for me, just, please.”
